title: Wendell and the Salt
premise: Freya Quintana carves bone charms that quiet the voices of the dead, hiding her gift in a valley where magic cannot follow. When the usurper King Aldric's witch-hunters breach the valley's protection, Freya flees with Wendell, an orphan boy who carries a shard of the old covenant stone, toward the free cities. Along the road she gathers a found family of outcasts, each marked by the hunt, and learns the covenant between the living and dead realms was broken by Aldric himself to steal his crown. In the besieged free city of Vaelmoor, Freya must sacrifice her own silence, letting every dead voice flood through her, to reforge the covenant and turn the tide, winning justice for the gifted at the cost of never hearing silence again.
about_author: Juniper Dunmore is the pen name of a former mortuary archivist who spent a decade cataloguing unclaimed remains before turning to fiction. She writes fantasy about grief, survival, and the stubborn families we build from strangers.

chapters.title: The Valley That Forgets
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. She carves a memorial charm for a drowned child while hiding the whispers of the dead from her neighbors, establishing the valley's magic-dead peace and her careful invisibility. Emotional beat: the loneliness of a gift that must be buried alive.

chapters.title: Wendell at the Gate
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. A starving boy arrives claiming the valley's edge let him through when it shouldn't have; he clutches a warm shard of grey stone that hums when Freya touches it. Emotional beat: reluctant tenderness, the first crack in her isolation.

chapters.title: Proclamation of Ash
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Crown riders post Aldric's decree: all gifted are to be seized, their harbors hanged. The riders' bloodhound-mage sniffs at the valley border and finds it fraying. Emotional beat: dread arriving like weather; safety was always borrowed time.

chapters.title: What the Dead Remember
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. The dead reveal the shard is a fragment of the covenant stone Aldric shattered to seize the throne, and that Wendell's grandmother died hiding it. Hunters cross the border as the valley's magic fails. Emotional beat: fury and guilt, flight chosen before she's ready.

chapters.title: The Road of Small Mercies
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Freya and Wendell fall in with outcasts: Brannoc, a deserter soldier; Sefa, a hedge-witch healer; old Tam, who speaks to rivers. They shelter in a ruined waystation and begin, awkwardly, to become a household. Emotional beat: warmth kindling under threat.

chapters.title: Hunters' Lanterns
chapters.summary: Brannoc's POV. The group is ambushed by witch-hunters; Tam is taken and Sefa wounded. Freya uses her gift openly for the first time, questioning a dying hunter's corpse to learn Aldric seeks the shard to finish his ritual. Emotional beat: the price of survival paid in blood and betrayal of her own rules.

chapters.title: Vaelmoor Under Siege
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. The company reaches the free city just as Aldric's armies encircle it; the council of free cities fractures between surrender and defiance. Freya realizes only a reforged covenant can unite living defenders and dead ancestors. Emotional beat: claustrophobic hope inside walls about to break.

chapters.title: The Broken Covenant
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. In the city's bone-vault, Wendell's shard resonates with ancient remains, showing Freya the original covenant ceremony and what it demands: a living voice willing to carry both realms without shield or filter. Emotional beat: terror sharpening into resolve; she volunteers what no one should give.

chapters.title: Night of Ten Thousand Voices
chapters.summary: Freya's POV, climax. As the walls fail, Freya stands in the breach and lets the dead pour through her, reforging the covenant aloud while Wendell anchors the stone. Ancestral dead rise beside the defenders; Aldric's stolen power unravels and he falls. Emotional beat: agonizing transcendence, victory bought with her silence forever.

chapters.title: A Quieter Kind of Loud
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV, resolution. Weeks later, the free cities draft a charter protecting the gifted; Freya, never alone now but never overwhelmed by her family's care, teaches Wendell bone-carving. Emotional beat: bittersweet peace, found family as the true covenant kept.
